The study involved an examination of the rotor fixture assembly to understand its functionality under standard boundary conditions.
The fixture components were modeled in NX CAD.
Finite Element Analysis was conducted both before and after the Topology Optimization process using the Density-based method in ANSYS.
The objective was to optimize rotor fixture design for additive manufacturing to reduce weight and lead time.
The topology optimization process resulted in a 16.3% mass reduction for the solid model and 27.5% for the shell model while maintaining stiffness.
Metal additive manufacturing reduced lead time by 46% despite a 17% increase in cost compared to conventional machining.
The axial rotor is 2,501 mm long and weighs 2,445 kg.
The reaction force Ra on the bearing is 11,489.8 N, and Rb on the rotor fixture is 12,486.6 N.
60% of the dead weight is on the central pad, with 20% each on the side pads.
The yield strength of steel, the chosen material for the rotor fixture, is typically around 250 MPa.
The maximum stress value for the new solid body design is 9.8341 MPa, and the maximum deformation is 0.00275 mm.
The maximum stress value for the new shell body design is 27.487 MPa, and the maximum deformation is 0.00709 mm.
Conventional machining cost for the rotor fixture is €9,450 with a lead time of 63 days.
Metal Additive Manufacturing cost for the rotor fixture is €11,440, with a 46% reduction in lead time to 34 days.
The project involved the assessment of additive manufacturing by reducing the weight of the rotor fixture through topology optimization.
